tasks.definition_of_done: `opi-ai` defines IO-free `Credential`, three-state `CredentialSource`, secret-free `AuthDescriptor::StoreCredential`, and object-safe boxed-future `CredentialStore::{read, write, delete, probe}` contracts; the OAuth envelope preserves `base_url`, and backend failures remain distinct from missing entries. `opi-coding-agent` supplies injected OS-keychain, environment, resolver, and non-reentrant global-lock implementations using workspace-managed `keyring-core`, `fs4`, and `secrecy`. Keychain service `opi` stores a versioned v1 JSON envelope keyed by provider id; malformed/unknown envelopes return explicit errors and never become absence or env fallback. API keys may fall back to `EnvCredentialSource` when the backend is unavailable; persisted OAuth remains keychain-required. Every mutation uses `<user_config_dir>/opi/credential.lock`, performs acquire-then-re-read, and shares package-private unlocked backend operations so T2 refresh never recursively locks. `Credential` uses `SecretString`; legacy `AuthDescriptor::StaticApiKey` retains `SecretKey`; T2 exclusively owns `OAuthCredential`, `ResolvedAuth`, and their concrete HTTP bridge. Async outer doctor/list-model command paths await probe and pass only redacted state into synchronous formatting; collection status gating receives precomputed probe state because the descriptor itself cannot perform IO. Fake-backend/temp-root tests prove object safety, store behavior, envelope errors, env fallback, lock timeout, and provider-factory/listing/doctor/dispatch integration. They recursively scan the injected config root plus captured stdout, stderr, diagnostics, and formatted errors: only the secret-free lock may exist outside the fake keyring, and seeded API/access/refresh secrets and the serialized envelope never appear.

tasks.title: OAuth architecture and per-request auth re-resolution
tasks.definition_of_done: `opi-ai` defines object-safe boxed-future `OAuthProvider`, `LoginPresenter`, and `AuthResolver` contracts, `OAuthCredential` including `base_url`, `ResolvedAuth`, no-IO `StaticAuthResolver`, and explicit non-retryable `ProviderError::{CredentialNeeded, CredentialRevoked}` variants mapped through provider diagnostics and typed `AgentError` without string matching. `opi-coding-agent` implements `AuthSource::{Baked, Store, EnvOAuthToken}`, the production TUI presenter, and registered Anthropic/Codex PKCE plus Copilot device-code flows; RPC/JSON/non-interactive credential-needed handling is a typed diagnostic path, not an unused presenter or login trigger. PKCE verifies S256/state, loopback-only binding, timeout, mismatched-state rejection, and callback/manual cancellation races; device polling covers pending, slow-down, denial, expiry, timeout, and cancellation. The new production `/login` branch invokes the registry/presenter and writes only after success; `/logout` performs locked delete; neither existed before this task. Near-expiry refresh uses five-minute skew, bounded lock/HTTP timeouts, double-checking, post-failure re-read, and no partial write. Factory-built Anthropic OAuth uses Bearer plus the OAuth beta header; Copilot exchanges the GitHub token, derives per-credential base URL, and uses an explicit captured-header OpenAI Chat compatibility profile; Codex uses an explicit `OpenAiResponsesProvider` compatibility profile targeting `/codex/responses` with account-id/originator/beta/static headers, not the standard Responses endpoint or a new provider type. Task 14.3 adds that profile's dynamic session-id/x-client-request-id mapping. Every approved provider resolves auth inside each returned stream immediately before HTTP and exposes the secret only there. Missing auth before output propagates typed CredentialNeeded through agent_loop, Agent, and CodingHarness; interactive login success retries the same pending turn without a duplicate user message, while RPC/JSON/non-interactive emit provider-id plus `/login <provider>` remediation and fail without starting a login flow. Separate captured auth-invalid responses for Anthropic OAuth, Copilot Chat, and Codex Responses become typed non-retryable CredentialRevoked, end the turn, issue no later request, and never launch login/retry. Mock HTTP/fake-store/harness/subprocess tests cover exact URLs/headers, all three flows, command creation, refresh races/failures, precedence, logout, mode behavior, per-stream re-resolution, and complete secret redaction without real credentials or network calls.
